title: Simple question.
author: lostinmo79
selftext:
Hey all, quick question. I started this journey around the beginning of this year and I’m wondering if my stats look normal or bad. So far my net return has been slightly over 41%, and during my worst period my account was down slightly over 11%. Obviously my winners gain way more than my losers—almost 2x. For reference, the S&P only gained about 12% in the same period.

Do these numbers look decent?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: those look good, but nine months is one market and this year rewarded almost anything long. the number I'd look at is how many trades it took to get there. if it's 30 trades, a couple of big winners could be most of the 41%. if it's 300, it means a lot more. an 11% drawdown against that return is fine either way.

replies.author: lostinmo79
replies.body: I don't remember the exact amount but it's over 200

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: over 200 changes my read, that's enough trades that two lucky winners can't carry it. what it can't rule out is rules that happen to fit this year. the cheap check is running it forward on paper for a month or two without touching anything. that forward run is what Quantradin does, I built it, free, no real money at risk: quantradin.com

comments.author: TastyTrading
comments.body: I use ThetaPal to track my progress and keep my portfolio monitored with ai market scouts

comments.author: Manzoyto_Popl
comments.body: Do you track signals and confidence in real time, then compare them against the actual outcomes later?

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: They look strong, but nine months is too short to say much. Before drawing conclusions I'd check the trade count, whether the 41% is realized or includes open positions, how much of it came from a few trades, and the result net of fees against SPY on a risk-adjusted basis. A good year in a rising market can come from simply having more risk (leverage or concentrated positions), so compare drawdown and volatility with the index too. If your trades cluster around earnings or macro news, Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for those releases) is one source for checking how much of the return came from those dates.
